name: Bed Maker
label: Dischord
lede: Four DC lifers, one first show in February 2020, a pause nobody chose, and a debut LP that Dischord called an act of defiance.

eras.title: See what might happen
eras.text: Nobody in Bed Maker was new. The rhythm section had played together in Alarms & Controls, the guitarist made tape-and-field-recording music as Insect Factory, and the singer had been in DC punk since the late '80s. They got one show in before the world shut.

years.h: Arthur Noll and Vin Novara invite Jeff Barsky to jam
years.p: Bassist Arthur Noll and drummer [[Vin Novara|bfec86c6-f1ae-4915-ac83-c1806a929118]], old [[Alarms & Controls|2db28ba7-b327-4926-aff2-0838913e6b39]] bandmates, invite guitarist Jeff Barsky of [[Insect Factory|ed9de18b-efae-478c-bd07-bc17214a36b7]] to see what might happen.
years.xp: Noll also played in [[Light Beams|42b3e741-bdf8-402e-acdf-f73c2a491951]] and Kid Congo Powers' band. Novara drummed in [[The Crownhate Ruin|6c13db70-bd59-44a0-8c6a-eeb0d0c8f40d]] and [[1.6 Band|e3b548df-c063-4603-bac1-1b01fcf84ef2]]. Barsky also played in [[Time Is Fire|636587a0-55da-492f-9e22-b3d9cf7c35f4]].

years.p: Amanda MacKaye had sung in Desiderata, [[Routineers|16e1e50b-c155-479b-8b74-432c899e1520]] and Jury Rig, and co-founded Sammich Records, which put out [[Swiz|eea2f3d8-1e94-436c-ae66-4633f99f55be]], [[Soulside|de2e8176-32c2-4abe-b718-9392dffd8ffe]] and [[Shudder to Think|5a6e19e0-3ff0-4b3d-869e-3c539d6d8707]]. Her brother is [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]].

years.h: Bed Maker's first show, at Rhizome
years.p: Bed Maker plays its first show at Rhizome, the DC arts space.

years.h: Bed Maker stops as the pandemic hits
years.p: One month after its Rhizome debut, Bed Maker stops playing, as did most people, Dischord notes.

eras.title: An act of defiance
eras.text: Two and a half years later they came back and went straight to work on a record, split between a Maryland home studio and the Inner Ear basement where Dischord records have been made since the early '80s.

years.p: Bed Maker resumes playing shows after two and a half years off.

years.h: Full set filmed by hate5six, September 22, 2022
yt: Full set filmed by hate5six, September 22, 2022

q: An act of defiance to the horrors of the last four-plus years.
years.p: Bed Maker finished its debut LP with Ian MacKaye and [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]] at Inner Ear in 2023. Dischord released it May 31, 2024.
years.xp:
Earlier sessions ran with [[Mike Schleibaum|44059ab7-0b66-472a-87dc-db3557dcd1b7]] and Matt Michel at Viva Studios and at Schleibaum's home studio in Maryland. Ian MacKaye is singer Amanda MacKaye's brother, and Dischord's notes say the LP only exists thanks to family and many friends. Eleven songs, from Two Left Feet and Candy Striper's Confession to Miss Dickens and Pan-Pan; Ballad of Tokitae was the preview track.

Bandcamp Daily made it an Album of the Day, hearing tense, irregular grooves, disciplined noise and well-placed silence, and a line back to the [[Minutemen|d4ad0149-d8ae-4105-8009-0221fce9ff35]]'s stops and starts. The same review heard Amanda MacKaye singing about the everyday weight of women's oppression, with domestic labor as the image.

eras.title: Tightly wound
eras.text: Bed Maker's follow-up was two songs, "The Mark" and "What Boy Where", cut in two days, and the band took them on the road.

years.p: Bed Maker recorded The Mark and What Boy Where in two days at Tonal Park in October 2025. Dischord released the 7" September 11, 2026.
years.xp: Ian MacKaye and Don Godwin recorded the two songs on October 3 and 5, 2025. Dischord calls them tightly wound. Cover art is by Luna Novara, layout by [[Jason Farrell|f458f662-c72b-485b-9152-81eda8659fdb]].

years.p: Bed Maker plays Charlottesville on the 25th, Durham on the 26th, Hyattsville on the 27th and Harrisonburg on the 29th.
